decisions.summary: Each piece of a main session's walked clock is booked to the task whose next step waited on it; round 4's project-wide reading and the round-3 page-session-yields rule withdrawn.
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): Amendment (l) verbatim: 'a minute should count as blocking. When something else is waiting on it to be done before it can be started', replacing (k)'s reading.

decisions.id: L2 the clue recorded with the data
decisions.summary: 'Blocks: <feature> T<n> | T<n> | none' in a dispatch prompt, page brief or builder brief's STOP POINT block, written as 'blocks' on the Agent call's event lines and on the page session's Phase line; 'L7R_BLOCKS=' read from a command's text; the line added to builder-brief.md and the research-record brief rules.
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): (l): 'to the extent that we can pass that kind of context clues to our tooling when the data is collected, whether through environment variables or I don't even know what else'. Reading the variable from the command text because a hook cannot see the shell environment is the mechanism, not a narrowing; the templates carrying the line are what make future data carry it.

decisions.id: L3 GUESS defaults where no clue is given
decisions.summary: Main session's own turns and waits block the task its lines carry; a builder's time blocks its own task, else its waiter's; a run or review agent blocks its waiter's task (a background run only from when it is waited on); a page session or research pass blocks nothing. Each labeled GUESS in book.rs's doc.
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): (l): 'not something our tooling can inherently know ... it doesn't have to be 100% exact ... only 90% of the time are we correct ... basically fine'. Labeled defaults for the unclued case are the approximation (l) accepts; research defaulting to nothing is overridden by a Blocks: line, which (l)'s decide-between-implementations case is to carry.

decisions.id: L4a prefer task-blocking work over work blocking none
decisions.summary: Among several in flight, what blocks a task is preferred to what blocks none.
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): (l): work done in parallel that blocks nothing 'is really not blocking anything'; a piece is never taken from a blocked task by non-blocking work.

decisions.id: L4b each task its own piece (round 5's L4b, fixed)
decisions.summary: Every task with blocking work in flight that second is booked its own piece, its own work's ends-last one (each_task); while a session or builder is in its own time - a turn or run, and a session's waits on the GM or idle hours too - its background work blocking ANOTHER task blocks that task beside it (beside); 'Waited on, blocking no task' only where no task-blocking work is in flight. Round 7 restatements: Blocking minutes reads 'each second once per task it blocks'; beside's reach through GM waits and idle hours is stated (the code did so already); the new test row names three Blocks: T4 passes of different ends (pinning the within-task ends-last pick) and two unclued passes waited on alone (the ends-last one apart, 8 s); the older blocking-by-dependency row states the page-session test's re-expectation (the review's 4 s to T1).
decisions.why: Within, as round 6 ruled, and the restatements keep it so. (a) 'each second once per task it blocks' now agrees with each_task instead of contradicting it. (b) beside through the session's GM waits and idle hours is (l) as written: research a task waits on 'would be blocking even if there was a different unrelated task happening' - a session waiting on the GM or idle is likewise unrelated to whether T4's next step waits on its research; it does not touch amendment (i), since the GM's own rows keep their time and only T4's booking, a working-time row, is added. Stated behavior the code already had, not a new decision. (d) the three-pass case pins that the ends-last pick stays within one task's work, and the two-unclued-passes case is L5's apart booking where no task-blocking work is in flight - both test rows of the ruled behavior, figures labeled measured 2026-11-25. (e) closes round 6's wording note. Wording only, not a finding: line 52's 'met after a shorter and before one' reads garbled (presumably 'before a longer one'), and it names 'an unclued pass' then 'the two unclued passes'.

decisions.id: L4c two paths to one task in one second each booked
decisions.summary: Where one task's work is waited on directly and again inside a builder in the same second, each path is booked: a GUESS, an overstatement where it happens.
decisions.why: Within, unchanged in substance from round 6: an approximation inside one task's own blocking, labeled GUESS, of the kind (l) accepts ('it doesn't have to be 100% exact ... only 90% of the time are we correct ... basically fine'); erring toward counting a task's blocking drops nothing (l) asks for. Round 7 only drops 'the data has not shown' for 'where it happens', a wording change.

decisions.id: L5 work blocking no task named apart
decisions.summary: Where only work blocking no task is in flight, the piece is booked to that work on the header's 'Waited on, blocking no task' line by category, never in the blocking columns.
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): (l) says such work is not blocking; amendment (c) requires nothing silent, and a named line satisfies both.

decisions.summary: 'waiting: nothing in flight - a page session running, no monitor on it' blocks what the page session blocks: its brief's task, else nothing (apart).
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): The same dependency rule as L3 applied to an untracked wait; keeps the (j) class and books it by (l).

decisions.id: L7 window blocking as the sum over tasks; denominators
decisions.summary: The window's blocking is the sum over tasks, the landed tasks' sum beside it, the header saying it passes the clock; every blocking percentage is of that sum less the GM's rows (amendment (i)), never of the clock; the GM's rows show their share of the whole.
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): Checked against (i) by name: the GM's minutes stay out of every other percentage's denominator and his share is stated of the whole, as (i) asks ('those minutes should not be part of the denominator when calculating the other percentages'). Excluding work that blocks no task from a blocking denominator follows (l)'s definition of blocking; a denominator that is the sum over tasks keeps each table summing to 100 when that sum passes the clock, and the header names each column's denominator and that the sum passes the clock, so no percentage math is left to the GM. Consistent, and stays consistent once L4b is fixed.

Also qualify 'Round 1's questions': its unqualified 'Window clipping: the window is the question asked' still reads as the position round 2 struck. decisions.summary: Keep BACK= (default 48h, a GUESS knob); a landed task whose first task-starts.jsonl start precedes the read-back, or has none, is named in its heading and on a 'Cut at the read-back' line (none when nothing is cut), pinned by a_landed_task_started_before_the_read_back_is_named.

It is legitimate on two grounds from the GM's own purpose. (1) The feature's request asks for the data 'in ideally a relatively cheap way' (2026-11-19), and a bound on how far back is read serves that. (2) With the cut named on every run, in the task's own heading and on a report line, plus a knob to read further, the tool no longer gives a wrong answer: it gives a labeled partial one, so it is not a defect left, and amendment (c)'s 'never silent' holds. Note that rulings.md is empty, because the block cites the arbiter in prose and not as an ask: ruling. So 'the arbiter's ruling of round 4 letting the knob stand so named' is not shown in the bundle, and this ruling rests on the substance, not on that citation.

decisions.summary: Window clipping restated: the window's own tables (the rest, the whole window) are clipped to it and sum to 100 over the working time; a landed task's tables carry its whole time.
decisions.why: This now agrees with the Which tasks item and with amendment (i). The round-3 item is settled.

decisions.summary: The name 'task time breakdown' goes at each gatherer, found by five commands: phase_row(, 'event-log phase' across the tree, event_log_hooks::append, write_dated(, ledger::cost::. Each command's hits are listed, with the name or the reason a hit is not a gatherer.
decisions.why: Round 3's item is met: every gatherer listed now has a command. Three gaps are left, none of them a narrowing that blocks, all to fix in the section. (a) The second command passes --exclude-dir=pool, saying 'the pool holds no code'. grep excludes by directory basename, so this also skips the pool CRATE that bullet 1 lists (pool/src/cache/phases.rs). Say so, or exclude by path. (b) The block now reads task-starts.jsonl, and D2 books by it, but no command searches that file's writer and no line says why it is not a gatherer. (c) The heading says 'written or computed through', but no command searches the reader's callers. make feature-report computes timing columns from the same lines (FR-005), and its Makefile help is one of 'the makefile comments that describe the timing' the GM named, yet only task-time's and where-time's help get the name.

decisions.summary: 'the GM' and 'the GM away' keep their minutes and show a share of the whole. Every other percentage (the category tables, the per-target table, the biggest-blocking list) is of the working time (the whole less the GM's). A 'working' row and a header line state the GM's minutes, their share, and which denominator each column uses.
decisions.why: This matches the GM's words: mention the minutes and their share of the total, and keep them out of 'the denominator when calculating the other percentages'. Folding 'the GM away' in is within: it is the same wait for him past a cap. Minutes denominators do not move because GM time is never machine time, which is correct.

decisions.summary: 'waiting: nothing in flight' becomes a family of classes read on every run from the event log (page session unmonitored; after the Stop's work had ended; until a notification woke it; until the session started again), plus a residual 'unexplained, then a <event> line'.
decisions.why: The GM asked that the row 'automatically gets broken down in the future'. This does it on every run. The residual names the event that ended each piece, so it is not a silent 'other'.

decisions.summary: A page session takes a wait's piece only where nothing else is live; among builders, runs and agents the one that ends last keeps the piece (critical path); no 'several in flight' row.
decisions.why: The GM's sentence is about the research number only ('if they were running in parallel with other things ... that number would be misleading'). Making page sessions yield to anything else applies it to research as he said it. The rule that blocking happens only with nothing else in flight, applied to everything, is the coordinating session's reading, and request.md marks it 'not his words'. Keeping the existing critical-path rule for builders, runs and agents keeps behavior he did not ask to change, so it is no narrowing of what he asked, and it needs no ruling. The asymmetry also fits his purpose: research is a queue implementation need not wait for ('before we could proceed with implementation'), while a builder's, a run's or a review's end is what the waiter proceeds on.

decisions.summary: 'Nothing else in flight' is read as nothing else THAT PAGE SESSION'S WAITER waits on. A main session waiting on page sessions alone books the wait as research blocking even while another main session (another clone) was implementing.
decisions.why: The GM: 'if they were running in parallel with other things, including running in parallel with other tasks which were not research-based, then that number would be misleading because it would essentially imply that we spent half of our wall clock time waiting for research to be done before we could proceed with implementation'. His words are 'other things' and 'other tasks', and 'we' is the project, with no limit to one waiter. The block says it applies 'nothing else in flight' 'literally to page sessions', but in its mechanism the words become 'nothing else its waiter waits on'. That is an unlabeled narrowing. Sessions do overlap: the block reads every clone's logs and sums every main session's clock, and the GM's '458 minutes ... 20% of the total time' puts the total near 2,290 min in a day of 1,440. So when one session waits only on page sessions while another implements, research still takes the blocking, and the number still implies implementation waited on research. That is the case his sentence names, and the fix's purpose fails there. The 'Working at once' header shows concurrency for the whole window, but it leaves the research number unchanged and does not say how much of it overlapped other work. Nothing makes the wider reading impossible: the walk already knows every actor at every instant (at_once()). Also, 'measured cause' carries no measurement, and no after-figure on real logs shows how much of the 949 the fix removes, so whether the narrowing matters rests on a premise nobody measured. What it should say: research blocking only where no other actor in ANY session read was working, the rest named in its own row or stated beside research's blocking as the share that overlapped other work, pinned by a test with two sessions. Or, if the session holds the waiter-only reading, it is the GM's to decide (through escalation), not this section's to assume.

decisions.summary: The header adds 'Working at once': the window's minutes with none, one, two, three or more actors working together (at_once()).
decisions.why: A report line that serves (k) (showing what ran in parallel) and amendment (d)'s parallelism question. It changes no booking.

decisions.id: L4a prefer task-blocking work over work blocking none
decisions.summary: Among several in flight, what blocks a task is preferred to what blocks none.
decisions.why: (l): work done in parallel that blocks nothing 'is really not blocking anything'; a piece is never taken from a blocked task by non-blocking work.

decisions.id: L4b one owner per second across DIFFERENT tasks
decisions.summary: The walk gives each second of a main session's clock ONE owner even when that second blocks different tasks. Two cases in the blocks: (1) 'Among several in flight': among everything that blocks a task - any task - the second goes to the one that ends last; (2) 'Blocking minutes' / the defaults: the session's own turns and calls are its own and block the task its lines carry. So a research pass carrying 'Blocks: T4' gets no blocking for T4 while a builder for unrelated T5 runs longer, nor while the main session is in its own turn on T5; and the booking tests pin tasks + apart = each session's clock.
decisions.why: This contradicts (l)'s one concrete example word for word: 'that research would be blocking even if there was a different unrelated task happening in a different subagent at the same time', and its standard, 'a different standard than whether or not a different unrelated piece of work is able to be done at the same time'. It contradicts the section itself: (l)'s lead item books a piece 'never ... by what else ran', and both cases book T4's second by what else ran for T5. It is not the imprecision (l)'s 90% tolerance accepts (missing context clues): the clue is present and the rule discards it. And it leaves 'the window's blocking is the sum over tasks, which passes the clock where tasks ran side by side' true only across clones, never for tasks one session ran side by side (builder slots, bundles). Not a reopening of a settled block: the ends-last (critical) pick is untouched WITHIN one task's work, where it is right; what is new and judged here is the (l) build using it, and the own-turn rule, to choose BETWEEN tasks. The test row 'blocking by dependency' points the same way: with 'Blocks: T7' the page session takes all 10 s and the review's 4 s of blocking is gone - one owner per second over two task-blocking items (whether those are the same task cannot be told from the bundle). Required outcome: a piece's blocking for the task it blocks does not depend on what runs, or what the session does, for another task - in a second where several tasks each have blocking work in flight (or one is in the session's own turn), each of those tasks is booked its own (critical) piece; 'Waited on, blocking no task' takes a second only when no task-blocking work is in flight; the identity the tests pin is restated to match (the per-task sum may pass a session's clock), with a test of two tasks' blocking work in flight in one session. The mechanism is the builder's.

decisions.id: L5 work blocking no task named apart
decisions.summary: Where only work blocking no task is in flight, the piece is booked to that work on the header's 'Waited on, blocking no task' line by category, never in the blocking columns.
decisions.why: (l) says such work is not blocking; amendment (c) requires nothing silent, and a named line satisfies both.

decisions.summary: 'waiting: nothing in flight - a page session running, no monitor on it' blocks what the page session blocks: its brief's task, else nothing (apart).
decisions.why: The same dependency rule as L3 applied to an untracked wait; keeps the (j) class and books it by (l).

decisions.id: L7 window blocking as the sum over tasks; denominators
decisions.summary: The window's blocking is the sum over tasks, the landed tasks' sum beside it, the header saying it passes the clock; every blocking percentage is of that sum less the GM's rows (amendment (i)), never of the clock; the GM's rows show their share of the whole.
decisions.why: Checked against (i) by name: the GM's minutes stay out of every other percentage's denominator and his share is stated of the whole, as (i) asks ('those minutes should not be part of the denominator when calculating the other percentages'). Excluding work that blocks no task from a blocking denominator follows (l)'s definition of blocking; a denominator that is the sum over tasks keeps each table summing to 100 when that sum passes the clock, and the header names each column's denominator and that the sum passes the clock, so no percentage math is left to the GM. Consistent, and stays consistent once L4b is fixed.

decisions.summary: A start no stop follows ends at the agent's last own call before its next start (flight.rs span_end), at the window's end only with no call at all; where-time's agent minutes move with the shared reader; a live long call understated by at most that call, labeled GUESS.
